Lappen Recorder includes third-party software. The project license does not
replace the licenses and copyright notices listed here. Source archives for
the native GPL components are attached to every Lappen Recorder release.

## Native recording components

- Source commit: `07a28338a871bdf7e0d24cdae65ce16e9470f2fa`

### OBS Studio (Warcraft Recorder fork) 27.2.0-4590-g71eaeafa4

- Source commit: `71eaeafa48785c13857a59e147316abad90cc364`

### FFmpeg n7.1.1

- Source repository: https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg
- Source commit: `db69d06eeeab4f46da15030a80d539efb4503ca8`
- Release source archive: `FFmpeg-n7.1.1-source.zip`

OBS Studio and the GPL-enabled FFmpeg build are distributed under the GNU
General Public License, version 2 or later. The shipped FFmpeg build enables
GPL code and libx264. See the project `LICENSE`, the matching release source
archives, and the upstream repositories for the complete terms and notices.

The npm package metadata for `noobs@0.0.201` identifies LGPL-2.0, while the
linked OBS components are GPL-covered. Lappen Recorder therefore treats the
combined native recording component as GPL-covered for distribution.

principal author, although it includes many contributions from others.

National Research Initiatives (CNRI, see http://www.cnri.reston.va.us)
in Reston, Virginia where he released several versions of the
software.

In May 2000, Guido and the Python core development team moved to
BeOpen.com to form the BeOpen PythonLabs team.  In October of the same
year, the PythonLabs team moved to Digital Creations, which became
Zope Corporation.  In 2001, the Python Software Foundation (PSF, see
https://www.python.org/psf/) was formed, a non-profit organization
created specifically to own Python-related Intellectual Property.
